title: Moda & Fenerbahçe Park: Local Asian-Side Afternoon Walk
seoTitle: Moda & Fenerbahçe Park: Asian-Side Istanbul Walk Guide
metaDescription: Ride the T3 nostalgic tram through Kadıköy and Moda, find coffee roasters and tea gardens, walk to Fenerbahçe Park, and catch sunset.
quickAnswer: Pairing Kadıköy's Moda peninsula with leafy Fenerbahçe Park makes one of Istanbul's most rewarding local afternoon walks. Ride the nostalgic T3 tram loop up from Kadıköy Pier, stop at Moda's specialty coffee roasters, ice cream counters, and seaside tea gardens, then follow the flat coastal path past Kalamış Marina to Fenerbahçe Park for open Marmara sunset views.

body.text: How does the nostalgic T3 tram loop through Kadıköy and Moda?

The [T3 Kadıköy–Moda nostalgic tram](https://www.rayist.com.tr/en/lines/istanbul-t3.html) runs a single-direction, 2.6-kilometre loop with 10 stops connecting Kadıköy Pier, Altıyol, pedestrian Bahariye Street, and Moda Avenue. Trains operate roughly from 07:10 to 21:00 using standard Istanbulkart fares, completing the full circuit in about 20 minutes.

Because the line runs clockwise, boarding near Kadıköy İDO Pier carries you uphill past the famous Bull Statue at Altıyol and along Bahariye's bookshops and theatres, then drops you right into the heart of Moda at Moda Caddesi or Moda İlkokulu. Check live schedules via [Istanbul Metro timetables](https://www.rayist.com.tr/en/istanbul-metro-timetables.html) if timing a short connection from the [Şehir Hatları Kadıköy ferry](https://sehirhatlari.istanbul/en/timetables). Even if you prefer walking, hopping on the T3 saves the initial uphill climb from the ferry docks.
Where are Moda's best specialty coffee roasters, ice cream shops and tea gardens?

Moda's residential side streets hold Istanbul's densest cluster of independent third-wave coffee roasters, historic ice cream parlours, and cliffside tea gardens. Start near Moda Caddesi and Caferağa lanes for espresso and pastries, then drift south toward Moda Aile Çay Bahçesi (Moda Family Tea Garden) overlooking the water.

Longstanding local favourites include Dondurmacı Ali Usta on the corner of Moda Caddesi—famous for seasonal fruit sorbets and thick dondurma queues on warm evenings—and dozens of small-batch roasters tucked along Nail Bey, Şair Nefi, and Dr. Esat Işık streets. Rather than sitting on the busiest main corner, wander two streets west toward the shoreline to find quiet courtyard cafés and vintage vinyl shops.

At the southern edge of the headland, the old Moda Pier (Moda İskelesi) houses a restored public library and café directly over the water, while the shaded tea gardens just above the sea wall serve simple tulip glasses of Turkish tea and toasted tost sandwiches with unobstructed views toward the historic peninsula.
How do you walk or bike out to Fenerbahçe Park?

Walking from Moda Pier to Fenerbahçe Park takes 35 to 45 minutes along a completely flat, paved waterfront promenade skirting Yoğurtçu Park and Kalamış Marina. Dedicated coastal cycling lanes also allow an easy 12-to-15-minute ride if you rent a municipal bicycle along the shore.

body.text: Fenerbahçe Park occupies a small green peninsula jutting into the Sea of Marmara beside the historic Fenerbahçe Lighthouse. Inside, wide shaded paths wind past century-old pistachio and pine trees, resident park cats, and municipal cafés overlooking the water. Because cars are kept away from the outer rim, it feels remarkably peaceful even on summer weekends.
What time gives the best Marmara sunset views?

Plan to reach Fenerbahçe Park's western seawall or Moda's coastal lawn 45 minutes before official sunset. That window catches golden light illuminating Sultanahmet's minarets across the Marmara horizon, followed by purple twilight over the Princes' Islands to the south.

In late autumn and winter (November through February), sunset falls between 17:30 and 18:30, making it easy to pair an early afternoon Moda coffee stroll with dusk views before heading back to Kadıköy Market for dinner. In June and July, sunset pushes past 20:15, so locals often start their walk around 17:30 to avoid peak afternoon sun along the exposed marina stretch.

items: Arrive in Kadıköy via Şehir Hatları ferry from Eminönü, Karaköy, or Beşiktaş for the best harbour approach.
Tap an Istanbulkart for the T3 tram uphill to Moda, then walk downhill and along the coast.
Bring a light layer for the sea breeze at Fenerbahçe Park after sunset.
Return to Kadıköy Çarşı (the market quarter) by short taxi or coastal walk for casual meze, tantuni, or fish.

faq.q: How long should I budget for the Moda and Fenerbahçe Park walk?
faq.a: Set aside three to four hours at a relaxed pace. That allows time for the T3 tram, a coffee or ice cream stop in Moda, the coastal stroll past Kalamış Marina, and sunset inside Fenerbahçe Park.

faq.q: Is the walk from Moda to Fenerbahçe Park flat and accessible?
faq.a: Yes. Once you descend from Moda Avenue to the shoreline, the entire coastal promenade through Yoğurtçu Park, Kalamış, and Fenerbahçe Park is flat and paved.

faq.q: Are there restrooms and cafés inside Fenerbahçe Park?
faq.a: Yes. Municipal cafés (İBB Sosyal Tesisleri and tea gardens) operate inside the park with seating overlooking the Marmara Sea and public restrooms nearby.

faq.q: Can I take a ferry directly to Moda?
faq.a: Moda Pier is mainly used as a cultural café and library space with limited seasonal sea-bus or ferry calls; the reliable year-round ferry hub is Kadıköy Pier, 15 minutes away on foot or via the T3 tram.

faq.q: What is the easiest way back to the European side after sunset?
faq.a: Walk or take a 10-minute taxi from Fenerbahçe Park back to Kadıköy Pier for frequent ferries to Karaköy, Eminönü, and Beşiktaş, or walk 15 minutes inland to Feneryolu Marmaray station for the cross-Bosphorus train.
